newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Sharansky checkmates chess champ.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Sharansky checkmates chess champ.

text.p: Former Soviet Jewish dissident Natan Sharansky, a big winner in Israeli elections in May, has won again -- this time in a chess match against grand master Gary Kasparov.
Sharansky, Israel's 48-year-old trade minister, ascribed his victory in Tuesday's match to the years he spent playing the game in his mind while in solitary confinement in Soviet prisons.

Kasparov, in Jerusalem for the start of the Israeli chess finals, played 25 matches simultaneously with public figures and chess players. He won 18, tied four and lost to Sharansky and two other players.

Sharansky, freed in an East-West prisoner swap in 1986 and given a hero's welcome in Israel, heads the Yisrael Ba-Aliya immigrants party which won a surprising seven seats in its first try for the 120-member Knesset in May.
"When I was young I played a lot and I even dreamt of being the world champion," Sharansky told Israel Radio in an interview broadcast on Wednesday.
"In prison, especially in isolation, when I had nothing, including chess obviously...I played in my head by myself. It helped," he said.
Asked by Israel Television if the victory would further his political career, Sharansky joked: "Oh sure. It could be another 200,000 voters will want to vote for me."
